title: How do I grab the last N seconds of a video in FFmpeg?
fullTitle: FFmpeg -sseof -3 With -c copy Returns 100 Frames, Not 90

scenes.narration: You want the last three seconds of a clip. So you put dash s s e o f, minus three, before dash i. What exactly comes out? Is it three seconds, and is it the frames you expect? We count the frames.

The source is ten seconds at thirty frames a second: three hundred frames, each with its own code. It is stored three ways: F F V one, where every frame is a keyframe, and lossless x two six four with a keyframe every one hundred frames, or every ten. Reader one is f f probe packets. Reader two decodes: frame hashes and pixel codes.
captions: 300 frames, 10 s, each frame has a code.

scenes.narration: Re-encoded, it is exact. Ninety frames, source frames two hundred ten to two hundred ninety nine, three seconds, on all three files. The control is dash s s, seven, which is ten minus three. It gives the same ninety frames.

Add dash c copy, and with a keyframe every one hundred frames you get one hundred frames. Three point three three three seconds, starting at keyframe two hundred. Ten more than you asked for. With a keyframe every ten frames, it is exactly ninety. At minus two point nine, the re-encode gives eighty seven frames, and copy gives ninety.

The offset counts back from the container duration, not from the picture. A ten second picture with twelve seconds of audio: minus three keeps three seconds of audio, but only one second of picture, thirty frames. And minus thirty on a ten second file is not an error. You get all three hundred frames.
captions: 10 s picture, 12 s audio: 1 s of picture.

scenes.narration: To get exactly the last N seconds, re-encode. With dash c copy, expect the start to move back to a keyframe. Not tested: other containers and encoders, real footage, and any player.
